hook: A GCC-rich sequence boosts protein translation starting at non-AUG codons in mammals.
summary: Cells sometimes start making proteins at codons other than AUG, but the rules are unclear. Cell-free and reporter assays identified a GCC-rich motif, NAT1, that enhances this initiation, while eIF1 and 5MP suppress it. Genome analysis shows such sites are depleted in human 5' UTRs. Links to disease genes and repeat-associated translation are suggestive, not shown directly.
title: Evolutionarily reinforced GC-rich motif enables non-AUG translation in mammals under eIF1/5MP-mediated fidelity control.
